Choosing the Right Database
• 	We have a lot of managed databases on AWS to choose from
• 	Questions to choose the right database based on your architecture:
• 	Read-heavy, write-heavy, or balanced workload? Throughput needs? Will it
change, does it need to scale or fluctuate during the day?
• 	How much data to store and for how long? Will it grow? Average object size?
How are they accessed?
• 	Data durability? Source of truth for the data ?
• 	Latency requirements? Concurrent users?
• 	Data model? How will you query the data? Joins? Structured? Semi-Structured?
• 	Strong schema? More flexibility? Reporting? Search? RDBMS / NoSQL?
• 	License costs? Switch to Cloud Native DB such as Aurora?
© Stephane Maarek
NOT FOR DISTRIBUTION © Stephane
 Maarek
 www.datacumulus.com
Database Types
• 	RDBMS (= SQL / OLTP): RDS, Aurora – great for joins
• 	NoSQL database – no joins, no SQL : DynamoDB (~JSON), ElastiCache (key / value
pairs), Neptune (graphs), DocumentDB (for MongoDB), Keyspaces (for Apache
Cassandra)
• 	Object Store: S3 (for big objects) / Glacier (for backups / archives)
• 	Data Warehouse (= SQL Analytics / BI): Redshift (OLAP), Athena, EMR
• 	Search: OpenSearch (JSON) – free text, unstructured searches
• 	Graphs: Amazon Neptune – displays relationships between data
• 	Ledger: Amazon Quantum Ledger Database
• 	Time series: Amazon Timestream
• 	Note: some databases are being discussed in the Data & Analytics section

• 	Manual DB Snapshot for longer-term recovery
• 	Managed and Scheduled maintenance (with downtime)
• 	Support for IAM Authentication, integration with Secrets Manager
• 	RDS Custom for access to and customize the underlying instance (Oracle & SQL Server)
• 	Use case: Store relational datasets (RDBMS / OLTP), perform SQL queries, transactions

## Match the data model to the query

Relational engines suit relationships, joins, flexible SQL and transactional constraints when those are core requirements. Key-value designs suit well-defined access patterns and horizontally scalable key-based operations.

### Reasoning and trade-offs

The explicit SQL and transaction requirements favor a relational engine. Other services may support particular pieces but would require substantial application redesign. Availability and scaling modes are subsequent engine-specific decisions.

### Avoid this trap

No database choice is automatically best because it is serverless or newer. Evaluate query patterns, consistency, transaction boundaries, operational effort and total cost together.

### Apply it

A finance application needs multi-row transactional updates and frequent ad hoc SQL joins across several entities. Which initial choice best matches the stated needs?

**Recommended design:** Use an appropriate managed relational engine such as RDS or Aurora.

The explicit SQL and transaction requirements favor a relational engine. Other services may support particular pieces but would require substantial application redesign. Availability and scaling modes are subsequent engine-specific decisions.

## Specialized databases and analytical boundaries

A graph database is suited to relationship traversal, such as finding connection paths or fraud rings. Its advantage depends on traversal-heavy queries rather than simply storing any data with identifiers.

### Reasoning and trade-offs

Relationship-centric traversal is the graph use case. The alternatives provide storage, delivery or transport abstractions without the required graph query model. Validate supported graph languages and actual traversal performance.

### Avoid this trap

Graph storage does not replace a warehouse for large analytical aggregations or a cache for repeated lookups. Choose a specialized database for a demonstrated query need.

### Apply it

A fraud team repeatedly explores several hops of relationships among accounts, devices and payment instruments. Which managed database category should be evaluated?

**Recommended design:** A graph service such as Amazon Neptune for relationship traversal.

Relationship-centric traversal is the graph use case. The alternatives provide storage, delivery or transport abstractions without the required graph query model. Validate supported graph languages and actual traversal performance.
